verdict.rationale: Homebrew's own docs cover headless and automated use. They document `NONINTERACTIVE=1` installs, unattended `.pkg` MDM installs, scriptable `brew bundle check || brew bundle install`, use in CI services such as GitHub Actions, and `as-console-user install --yes` for scheduled jobs with no logged-in user. One community comment calls Homebrew brittle on CI, but it gives no concrete failure, so it lowers confidence rather than creating a dispute. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of reliable CI runs, and a dedicated CI or headless guide (e.g. caching or official CI actions).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: one command can set up project dependencies across these environments and in continuous-integration services such as GitHub Actions.
You can use this behaviour in scripts like so: brew bundle check || brew bundle install
Use this in administrative scripts and scheduled jobs to manage an existing installation, including when no user is logged in.
If you're on macOS, try our `.pkg` installer for interactive or unattended MDM installs.
